dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:801.text: To hold something in the mouth. Formed from 口, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:802.text: To hold and savor a flavor in the mouth. Formed from 口, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:803.text: To taste. Formed from 口, with 叕 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a mouth or beak.

shuowen:804.text: To chew. Formed from 口, with 集 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 集.

shuowen:805.text: To taste. Formed from 口, with 齊 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “The Grand Protector received the cup, made the offering and tasted it.”

shuowen:806.text: To bite or chew. Formed from 口, with 焦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:807.text: To suck. Formed from 口, with 允 indicating the sound.

shuowen:808.text: To drink a little. Formed from 口, with 率 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 㕞.

shuowen:809.text: To sip a little. Formed from 口, with 毚 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a mouth or beak.

shuowen:810.text: To eat; a mouth or beak. Formed from 口, with 筮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:811.text: To eat. Formed from 口, with 臽 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 含.

shuowen:812.text: To eat a little. Formed from 口, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:813.text: The appearance of chewing. Formed from 口, with 尃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:814.text: To hold in the mouth, 嗛. Formed from 口, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:815.text: To chew food. Formed from 口, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:816.text: Flavor. Formed from 口, with 未 indicating the sound.

shuowen:817.text: The exclamation 嚛 when eating something pungent. Formed from 口, with 樂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:818.text: A mouth full of food. Formed from 口, with 窡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:819.text: Breath released after eating one's fill. Formed from 口, with 意 indicating the sound.

shuowen:820.text: To pant. Another explanation: to be joyful. Formed from 口, with 單 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The black-maned white horses pant.”

shuowen:821.text: Liquid in the mouth, saliva. Formed from 口, with 𡍮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:822.text: In Nanyang, a great shout is called 咦. Formed from 口, with 夷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:823.text: The Eastern Yi call breathing 呬. Formed from 口, with 四 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The 犬夷 have come to rest.”

shuowen:824.text: Rapid breathing. Formed from 口, with 耑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:825.text: To breathe outward. Formed from 口, with 乎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:826.text: To breathe inward. Formed from 口, with 及 indicating the sound.

shuowen:827.text: To blow. Formed from 口, with 虛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:828.text: To blow, 噓. Formed from 口 and 欠.

shuowen:829.text: A deep sigh. Formed from 口, with 胃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:830.text: Breath from the mouth. Formed from 口, with 𦎫 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The great carriage moves 啍啍.”

shuowen:831.text: A release of breath on becoming aware, a sneeze. Formed from 口, with 疐 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “When I long for you, I sneeze.”

shuowen:832.text: A term used in rustic speech. Formed from 口, with 質 indicating the sound.

shuowen:833.text: A mouth constrained in speaking. Formed from 口, with 金 indicating the sound.

shuowen:834.text: The mouth closed. Formed from 口, with 禁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:835.text: To identify oneself. Formed from 口 and 夕. 夕 means darkness; in darkness people cannot see one another, so they use their mouths to name themselves.

shuowen:836.text: I: a self-designation. Formed from 口, with 五 indicating the sound.

shuowen:837.text: Knowledge or wisdom. Formed from 口, with 折 indicating the sound.

shuowen:838.text: Honored or exalted. Formed from 尹; because one issues commands, it also contains 口.

shuowen:839.text: To command. Formed from 口 and 令.

shuowen:840.text: To deliberate on affairs is called 咨. Formed from 口, with 次 indicating the sound.

shuowen:841.text: To call, 𧦝. Formed from 口, with 刀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:842.text: To inquire. Formed from 口, with 門 indicating the sound.

shuowen:843.text: To assent. Formed from 口, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:844.text: To lead. Formed from 口, with 昌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:845.text: To respond to one another. Formed from 口, with 禾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:846.text: To laugh heartily. Formed from 口, with 至 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “They laugh heartily.”

shuowen:847.text: To laugh. Formed from 口, with 亞 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Laughing and speaking, 啞啞.”

shuowen:848.text: To laugh heartily. Formed from 口, with 豦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:849.text: To laugh. Formed from 口, with abbreviated 稀 indicating the sound. Another explanation: grief without tears is called 唏.

shuowen:850.text: The appearance of laughter. Formed from 口, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:851.text: Much speech. Formed from 口, with 世 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Do not chatter so.”

shuowen:852.text: A repeated sound written 𡂢𡂢, whose quality is not further explained. Formed from 口, with 䲷 indicating the sound. [The descriptive sense is uncertain.]

shuowen:853.text: To address one another. Formed from 口, with 出 indicating the sound.

shuowen:854.text: To answer. Formed from 口, with 矣 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 埃.

shuowen:855.text: A pause or interval in speech. Formed from 口, with 𢦔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:856.text: To gather and talk. Formed from 口, with 尊 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Gathering to gossip, hating behind one's back.”

shuowen:857.text: Whispered speech. Formed from 口 and 耳. The Odes says: “Whispering and turning things about.”

shuowen:858.text: To suck or sip. Formed from 口, with 甲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:859.text: A small sound. Formed from 口, with 彗 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Tiny are those little stars.”

shuowen:860.text: The sound of speech. Formed from 口, with 然 indicating the sound.

shuowen:861.text: To laugh heartily. Formed from 口, with 奉 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 菶菶 in the Odes' “Melons and little melons flourish.”

shuowen:862.text: Abundant vigor or breath. Formed from 口, with 眞 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Marshaling the troops, 嗔嗔.”

shuowen:863.text: Swift. Formed from 口, with 𤐫 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The carriage does not rush.”

shuowen:864.text: To cry out, 唬. Formed from 口, with 虖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:865.text: A sound going 喅喅. Formed from 口, with 昱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:866.text: A blowing or whistling sound. Formed from 口, with 肅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:867.text: Pleased. Formed from 口, with 㠯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:868.text: Joy. Formed from 口, with 䍃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:869.text: To open. Formed from 戶 and 口.

shuowen:870.text: A sound. Formed from 口, with 貪 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Noisy are those bringing field meals.”

shuowen:871.text: All; entirely. Formed from 口 and 戌; 戌 means entirely.

shuowen:872.text: Level or even. Formed from 口, with 壬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:873.text: To assist. Formed from 口 and 又.

shuowen:874.text: Used in the expression 不啻 in speech. Formed from 口, with 帝 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 啻 means 諟, to affirm. Pronounced like 鞮. [The first gloss is elliptical.]

shuowen:875.text: Good. Formed from 士 and 口.

shuowen:876.text: Close or dense. Formed from 用 and 口.

shuowen:877.text: Grandiose speech. Formed from 口, with 庚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:878.text: Who. Formed from 口 and 𢏚, with 又 indicating the sound. 𢏚 is the ancient form of 疇.

shuowen:879.text: To hold deeply in the mouth. Formed from 口, with 覃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:880.text: Food becoming stuck. Formed from 口, with 壹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:881.text: To swallow. Formed from 口, with 𥁕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:882.text: To spit out without retching. Formed from 口, with 見 indicating the sound.

shuowen:883.text: To discharge. Formed from 口, with 土 indicating the sound.

shuowen:884.text: Breath moving contrary to its course. Formed from 口, with 歲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:885.text: To oppose. Formed from 口, with 弗 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Oppose their elders.”

shuowen:886.text: The appearance of unsettled speech. Formed from 口, with 憂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:887.text: Speech halting and difficult. Formed from 口, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:888.text: Desire: to like something. Formed from 口, with 耆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:889.text: To chew and eat. Formed from 口, with 炎 indicating the sound. Another form is 噉.

shuowen:890.text: Speech obstructed by the tongue. Formed from 口, with 更 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 綆, a well rope.

shuowen:891.text: Boastful speech. Formed from 口, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:892.text: 啁 means boastful speech, 嘐. Formed from 口, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:893.text: A flattering tone. Formed from 口, with 圭 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 醫.

shuowen:894.text: Speech in mutual rebuke and resistance. Formed from 口 opposed to 䇂; 䇂 is an unpleasant sound. Pronounced like 櫱.

shuowen:895.text: 讘吺: much speech. Formed from 口, with abbreviated 投 indicating the sound.

shuowen:896.text: To censure harshly. Formed from 口, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:897.text: To censure harshly. Formed from 口, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:898.text: To obstruct. Formed from 口, with 庶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:899.text: Reckless or false speech. Formed from 口, with 夾 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 莢.

shuowen:900.text: Much speech. Formed from 口, with 盍 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 甲.
